passage:
After a storm cut electricity, phones slowly ran out of battery. Mia's family used a small emergency radio to hear weather updates.
Mia had thought the radio was old-fashioned. That night, it became the most important object in the house.
The announcer gave information about closed roads, shelters, and when power might return.
When electricity came back, Mia's father checked the batteries and put the radio back into the emergency bag.
The storm taught Mia that older technology can still matter. A device does not need to be modern to be useful. In an emergency, simple and reliable may be better than smart and fragile.
